chunks: Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Hormozi al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu al-Hasan Dawood al-Bakri say, I heard Ali ibn Da'bal ibn Ali al-Khuza'i say,

When my father was approached by death, his color changed, his tongue became tied, and his face turned black. I was about to return from his religion (or school of thought), but I saw him after three days in what the sleeper sees (in dreams), wearing white clothes and a white cap. I said to him, 'O father, what has God done to you?'

He said, 'O son, what you saw of the blackening of my face and the tying of my tongue was because of my drinking wine in the abode of this world. I remained in that state until I met the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and he was wearing white clothes and a white cap.'

He said to me, 'Are you Da'bal?' I said, 'Yes, O Messenger of God.' He said, 'Then recite to me your words regarding my sons.' So I recited my words: 'May God not let the age laugh if it laughs one day, and the Household of Ahmad are oppressed. They have been subdued, scattered, exiled from the threshold of their home, as if they had committed what is not forgiven.'
He said, 'He said to me, 'You have done well.' Then he interceded for me and gave me his clothes, and here they are,' and he pointed to the clothes on his body.
ai.seo_question: What was the sign of Ali ibn Da'bal's sin and how did the Prophet forgive him?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the poetic merit of Ali ibn Da'bal, a key figure in transmitting the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt, illustrating the Shia belief in the intercessory power of the Prophet's recognition of their defenders. The dream vision serves as a spiritual validation of his lifelong dedication to chronicling the sufferings of the Imams, specifically their displacement and oppression. The gift of the Prophet's white garments symbolizes purity and the removal of the spiritual stains caused by his consumption of wine, linking personal piety with dynastic loyalty.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 66-36 Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Hormozi al-Bayhaqi narrated that he had heard Abal Hassan Dawood al-Bakri say that he had heard (De’bel’s son) Ali ibn De’bel ibn Ali al-Khoza’ee say,

“When my father was about to die he changed colors, could not talk and his face turned black. I was about to quit following his religion (Islam), but after three days which passed like this I saw my father in my dreams wearing a white robe with a white cap on his head. I asked him, ‘O father! What has God done to you?’

He replied, ‘O son! When you saw my face turn dark and my tongue stopped from talking, it was because I used to drink wine in this world. I was that way until once I met God’s Prophet (S) (here in the Hereafter) wearing a white robe with a white cap on his head.

Then he asked me, ‘Are you De’bel?’ I said, ‘Yes, O Prophet of God!’ Then the Prophet (S) said, ‘Recite to me the poem that you recited for my son Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.).’ Then I recited it:God will not let time laugh, if it were to laughWhile Ahmad’s Household are victims of injustice.Indeed were they subjected to oppressionAnd were ruthlessly thrown out of their homes;As if they had committed what cannot be forgiven.
Then God’s Prophet (S) told me, ‘Excellent!’ Then the Prophet (S) interceded on my behalf and gave me some of his clothes which you can see.’ He pointed to the clothes he was wearing.”
